summary: A well-built listening paper. All four parts have the right setting, length (610-880 words a script) and real distractors: corrections in Part 1, named-and-rejected options in Parts 2 and 3. Part 4 is slightly gentle because most gap words are said exactly as printed right after a date or number, but overall this is real IELTS standard.
strengths: Part 1 has five genuine traps (wrong date corrected, meadow price vs orchard price, old arrival time, cash dropped, posted letter replaced by text).
Part 2 and Part 3 MCQs mention every wrong option and reject it, as in the real test; the Part 3 multi-selects clear all three distractors explicitly.
Part 2 matching uses true paraphrase (burned down / rebuilt after a fire; a firm of joiners / a local business).
Answers appear in question order throughout; spelling and word limits are respected.
The Part 4 lecture is a coherent academic talk with clear signposting.

issues.problem: Evidence line 'was paid for by the people of this town' does not by itself point to 'most of the cost' or to fundraising events.
issues.change: Evidence changed to 'together raised more than three quarters of what we needed'.

issues.problem: Pair 'the ground in the orchard is very stony' / 'the ground is stony' was near-identical wording, not a paraphrase.
issues.change: Pair changed to ['anything I ought to bring', 'Must bring'].

issues.problem: Pair 'a class project at Northgate Primary' / 'a group of schoolchildren' was loose; the script has a closer paraphrase.
issues.change: Pair changed to ['a group of nine-year-olds', 'a group of schoolchildren'].

issues.problem: Pair 'nobody knew it was there' / 'discovered by accident' does not mean the same thing.
issues.change: Pair changed to ['digging out the foundations', 'during building work'].

issues.problem: 'invertebrates' is said word for word in the script, so 'the mayflies and the shrimps' is not the paraphrase students need.
issues.change: Pair changed to ['tells you what the water has been like', 'judge water quality'].

issues.problem: Pair repeated the answer word 'shadow' on both sides.
issues.change: Pair changed to ['told the time by watching', 'the time was read from'].

issues.problem: Pair 'what ended it' / 'made timetables impossible' paired two different ideas.
issues.change: Pair changed to ['What ended it', 'until the'] (X lasted until Y = Y ended X).

issues.problem: No paraphrase pair although a genuine one exists.
issues.change: Added: We allow no / Not allowed; stays open until eight in the evening / open until 8 pm; will reach you / sent by; set off / begin the trail; who wanted it / demanded by; a method of finding longitude / a longitude method; The navigation system in your telephone / navigation today.

issues.problem: Pair 'much quieter' / 'smaller and quieter' is close to identical, but the script offers no better paraphrase for this gap.
issues.change: Kept. Q1, Q3, Q4 and Q35 left without a pair (spelled name, numbers, verbatim date-anchored line).

issues.problem: Part 4 is a little gentle: nearly every gap word is spoken exactly as in the notes, often straight after a date (1656, 1714, 1927) that locates it instantly.
issues.change: For future sets, paraphrase more of the note lines around the gaps and avoid putting a date next to every gap.

issues.problem: Script (not changed): Part 3 has two consecutive lines by speaker A ('The photographs are worth more...' then 'So in the review we also have to say...'). Harmless; reported only.
issues.change: None needed; the audio is already recorded.
